findings.evidence: Identical `rw` chains at the end of `nonempty_edge` and `nonempty_compStruct`. Identical `refine ⟨yonedaEquiv.symm _, boundary.hom_ext fun j ↦ yonedaEquiv.injective ?_⟩; rw [boundary.ι_ι_assoc, stdSimplex.δ_comp_yonedaEquiv_symm, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]` in both the `| 0` and `| 1` branches.
findings.fix: Add a lemma in BoundaryColimits.lean, e.g. `boundary.eq_ι_comp_iff : σ₀ = ∂Δ[n+1].ι ≫ σ ↔ ∀ j, X.δ j (yonedaEquiv σ) = yonedaEquiv (boundary.ι j ≫ σ₀)`. Use it in all four places.
findings.issue: The same face-extraction step is repeated word for word: `have h (j) : X.δ j (yonedaEquiv σ) = v j := by rw [← stdSimplex.yonedaEquiv_δ_comp, ← boundary.ι_ι_assoc, ← hσ, hf.ι_desc, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]` appears in both `nonempty_edge` (l.76) and `nonempty_compStruct` (l.98). Its converse also appears twice in `isTerminalVertex_iff_of_isStrictSegal` (n=0 and n=1 branches): `boundary.hom_ext fun j ↦ yonedaEquiv.injective _; rw [boundary.ι_ι_assoc, stdSimplex.δ_comp_yonedaEquiv_symm, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]`. The reusable fact, that a simplex extends `σ₀` exactly when its faces are the faces of `σ₀`, is hidden.

findings.evidence: Mathlib exposes `isoNerve_hom_app_apply : ((isoNerve n).hom.app _ s).obj i = ULift.up (s i)` for exactly this purpose. The PR does not use it and relies on raw `rfl`.
findings.fix: Prove the object equality with Mathlib's `stdSimplex.isoNerve_hom_app_apply` (StdSimplex.lean:448) plus an `obj₀Equiv`/`nerveEquiv` simp lemma, or add a comment explaining why `rfl` is needed.
findings.issue: `(isoNerve n).hom.app _ (obj₀Equiv.symm (Fin.last n)) = nerveEquiv.symm (ULift.up (Fin.last n))` is closed by `ComposableArrows.ext₀ rfl`. This is an undocumented definitional unfolding through `NatIso.ofComponents`, `Equiv.toIso`, `objEquiv` and `nerveEquiv`, and it breaks if any of those wrappers changes.

summary: The proofs are mostly robust, but the same 'faces of an extension / extension from faces' reasoning is written out by hand four times instead of being factored into a lemma. `stdSimplex.isTerminalVertex_last` closes a key step with `rfl` through an undocumented definitional equality between `isoNerve` and `nerveEquiv`.
